w: A well-wisher came for Swamishri’s darshan. He explained that because of his business hassles there were problems and unhappiness in his family. He added, "My mother says our problems have arisen the day we brought the small murti of Ghanshyam Maharaj (Lalji) in the house." Swamishri advised, "By bringing God one does not invite pain and problems. One has to go through such situations because of one’s past karmas. God does good to all. The Lalji (murti) is your only support. Pray to Him but don’t doubt Him and blame Him. He has come to make you all happy and not unhappy. That is why people remember and worship God. Otherwise why should people remember Him? When our mind is not pure then our works may not be fulfilled."

Every night, before Swamishri retires to bed, he invariably comes out of his room to momentarily meet the sadhus and devotees waiting for him. Today, the volunteers of the housekeeping department were standing with dustbins, brooms and sweeping materials. As soon as Swamishri came out, one of them jokingly asked, "Swami, its been a month (since we’ve been doing service in the mandir) now, so we want our wages." Then the whole team chorused like a workers’ union, "Swami, give us our wages." Swamishri responded with humor, saying, "We should not set up a union but have unity. Our wages mean experiencing more peace within, remembering and singing God’s name and glory, progressing in our jobs or businesses and getting the pleasure and blessings of Shriji Maharaj, Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj. "Even while doing our service (seva) we should do each others work, and refrain from distinctions like ‘this is mine and this is his’. By doing it with ‘samp, suhradayabhav and ekta’ Yogiji Maharaj will be pleased..."

Cultural Program "Avasar Anandno" The evening Guru Bhakti Din assembly included a drama, a dance, inspiring incidents of volunteers, speeches by Viveksagar Swami and Dr Swami and finally capped by Swamishri’s blessings. The Governor of Georgia, Sonny Perdue, had sent a proclamation to honor Swamishri.

Two brothers requested Swamishri that he blesses them so that unity persists in their family. In response Swamishri stated, “Keep three ‘S’s in your lives: satsang, seva (service) and samp (unity). May the mutual feelings that you have now continue. Instil this sentiment in your children. Only then you will progress.”

Swamishri departed from Jhadeshwar at 10.10 am and arrived in Amdavad at 12.30 pm. During Swamishri’s stay Viveksagar Swami discoursed on the subject, “Chalo Chale, Ham Akshardham” in the daily evening assembly. Thereafter Swamishri blessed the assembly.

As Pramukh Swami Maharaj was getting up for his walk, his blood pressure was taken as usual. Today it was only 94. During the walk, Yogvivek Swami asked Swamishri in medical terms, "Even with such low blood pressure, you are walking? Outside, if a patient had such low blood pressure, he would not even be allowed to get out of bed. He would be made to rest; he would have to rest. He would not even be able to stand, and walking would be out of the question. Whereas you walk while talking with us."

In this very context, Yogicharan Swami said, "A few years ago Swamishri was in Navsari and had called a meeting about the construction of the Surat hospital. When his blood pressure was taken at that time, it was 50 over 20. Dr Kiran was also with us. He measured it a second and a third time and broke into a sweat, because if anything happened, there were no such medical facilities in Navsari. But Swamishri was perfectly fine. After a while he said, 'If the sadhus and devotees for the Surat hospital meeting have come, call them.' We said, 'How can a meeting be held in this condition?' Swamishri said, 'The poor people have all come from far away!' Dr Kiranbhai and everyone requested, 'You must rest now,' but Swamishri did not agree and held the meeting continuously for two hours. And the miracle was that nothing at all happened to him, no sweating, no blackouts, nothing."

When Pramukh Swami Maharaj was getting up for his walk, his BP was taken as usual. Today the BP came to only 94. During the walk, Yogvivek Swami asked Swamishri in medical terms, "Even though your BP is so low, you are walking? Outside, with such low BP, a patient would not even be allowed to get out of bed; he would be made to rest, he would have to rest. He would not even be able to stand, and he would certainly not be made to walk. Whereas you walk while talking with us."

In this connection Yogicharan Swami said, "A few years ago Swamishri was in Navsari and had called a meeting about the construction of the Surat hospital. At that time his BP was taken and it was 50 over 20. Dr Kiran was also with him. He measured it a second and third time and broke out in a sweat, because if something happened, there were no such medical facilities in Navsari, but Swamishri was quite well. After a while he said, 'If the sants and devotees for the Surat hospital meeting have arrived, call them.' We said, 'How can there be a meeting in this condition?' Swamishri said, 'The poor people have all come from far away!' Dr Kiranbhai and everyone requested, 'At this time you must only rest,' but Swamishri did not agree, and held the meeting continuously for two hours. And the miracle was that nothing happened to him at all, he did not sweat, he did not feel faint, nothing at all."
After finishing puja, quoting words from "Purushottam Bolya Prite," Mahant Swami Maharaj showered blessings in this way:
"If there is a supreme feeling and a sense of divinity, one moves at rocket speed. So revel in seeing divinity. Dive into the ocean of divinity. Divinity... divinity... divinity...

Whatever has happened until today is all forgiven. Open new account books and open an account of divinity on every page. Devotees should see divinity in one another. A supreme devotee has divinity filled in his shoulder bag, in his pockets, everywhere; no place is left empty. It is a matter of seeing divinity along with niyam and dharma. Divinity alone spoils everything. If someone breaks niyams, simply do not admire him, that is all, but certainly do not see fault in him. One may not be able to keep very strict niyams, but even if one has the desire to please Maharaj by keeping niyams, that too is good. Maharaj likes those who keep niyams very much."
Leaving the assembly, Swamishri sat for breakfast at his residence. Vivekjivandas Swami said:

"Meeting you and hearing your blessings, Shri Harshvadanbhai Trivedi, editor of the magazine 'Garavi Gujarat,' was deeply moved. When Harshvadanbhai came onto the stage for your blessings, you noticed his choti (tuft of hair) and said, 'He keeps a choti.' Hearing this he said, 'Mahant Swami Maharaj is like Bapa. Very sharp.' And after hearing the blessings he said, 'Swami gave very fitting examples, and graphical too.' He said, 'Divinity in the shoulder bag, in the pockets, all around.' And he also said, 'Whatever has happened until today is forgiven.' Only one who is divine can say this. He is very strong and focused. Nothing can disturb him."

ds.t: The elephant bows to the ant
w: Today, during Mahant Swami Maharaj's walk, Aksharatitdas Swami presented his newly written English children's storybook "Kidi and Mr Hathi" (the ant and Mr Elephant). He asked Swamishri, "Any correction in this?"
Swamishri said, "In the last scene of this, it shows the elephant taking the ant on its trunk and meeting it like that, but in truth the elephant bows to the ant and becomes like the ant; show that."
What a subtle but very important correction!
Aksharatitdas Swami's next book is on the atma. He requested Swamishri, "You too are a good artist, so we wish that you yourself draw a picture of the atma."
Swamishri agreed.

Sahajmunidas Swami, who helps in this work, asked, "Swami! The atma is formless; how can a picture of it be drawn?" Then, recalling the siddhant, the sadhus said, "Our atma is you, so it means drawing a picture of you, doesn't it! And we should say that our atma is Mahant Swami Maharaj, shouldn't we?"
"That is exactly what is to be understood," said Swamishri.
